 Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root Recalled Nationwide for Possible Salmonella
 By Bill Marler on November 18, 2026 
 Posted in Food Poisoning Information 
 Larbi Inc. of Valley Cottage, New York, is recalling three lots of Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root because the product may be contaminated with  Salmonella . The company announced the recall on November 17, 2026, and the  Food and Drug Administration posted the notice  the same day. No illnesses have been reported to date.
 Key facts 
 Company: Larbi Inc., Valley Cottage, New York (Herb To Body brand)
 Product: Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root C/S, 4 oz pouch
 Lots: HB02223, HB02474 and HB02848
 Hazard: possible  Salmonella  contamination, reported to Larbi by its ingredient supplier
 Where sold: nationwide, January to November 2026, through herbtobody.com, online marketplaces and retail stores
 Illnesses: none reported as of the November 17, 2026 announcement
 What is being recalled 
 Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root C/S (cut and sifted), 4 oz pouch
 Lot numbers HB02223, HB02474 and HB02848
 The lot number is printed below the barcode on the back label. The company says no other lots or products are affected.
 Where it was sold 
 The pouches were sold nationwide from January 2026 to November 2026 through herbtobody.com, third-party online marketplaces and retail stores. That is a sales window of roughly ten months for a shelf-stable dried herb, which means much of the product has likely already been used and some of it is still sitting in kitchen cabinets.
 How the problem was found 
 Larbi says its ingredient supplier notified it that an ingredient lot used in these products may be contaminated with  Salmonella . Larbi has stopped distributing the recalled lots and says it is working with the supplier and FDA.
 The notice does not name the supplier. A supplier notice of this kind usually goes to more than one customer, and without a name the public cannot tell which other brands received the same ingredient lot. It is worth watching for additional recalls.
 Why a dried herb can carry Salmonella 
 Salmonella  does not grow in dry products, but it survives in them for months or longer. Dried herbs, spices and botanicals have been the source of recalls and outbreaks before, and a dried root that is steeped in water that is not boiling, or stirred into food without a cooking step, has no kill step between the pouch and the person.
 Symptoms of Salmonella infection 
 Most people infected with  Salmonella  develop diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramps, usually six hours to six days after exposure, and most recover in four to seven days without treatment. The infection can be serious or fatal in young children, frail or elderly people and people with weakened immune systems, and in some cases the bacteria enter the bloodstream and cause more severe illness. Anyone who used this product and became ill should contact a health care provider and mention the recall.
 What consumers should do 
 Check any Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root pouch for lot HB02223, HB02474 or HB02848.
 Do not consume it. Throw it away; the company is offering a full refund.
 Wash hands, containers, tea infusers and surfaces that touched the product.
 Frequently asked questions 
 Which Herb To Body yellow dock root is recalled? 
 The 4 oz pouch of Herb To Body Yellow Dock Root C/S in lots HB02223, HB02474 and HB02848. The lot number is below the barcode on the back label.
 Where was the recalled yellow dock root sold? 
 Nationwide from January 2026 to November 2026, through herbtobody.com, third-party online marketplaces and retail stores.
 Has anyone gotten sick? 
 No illnesses had been reported when the recall was announced on November 17, 2026.
 Is it safe if I make tea with it? 
 No. The company and FDA say not to consume the product. Throw it away.
 I will update this post if the supplier is named or other products made with the same ingredient lot are recalled.
